content:
Yes, when you delete a virtual environment created with `pyenv` and the `pyenv-virtualenv` plugin using the `pyenv virtualenv-delete <venv-name>` command, it will completely remove the specified virtual environment. This includes all the packages installed in that environment, as well as the environment itself. 

The virtual environment is generally stored as a separate directory containing its own Python interpreter along with any libraries or packages you've installed into it. When you delete the environment using `pyenv virtualenv-delete`, you're effectively removing this directory and all its contents. Therefore, nothing that was installed in the virtual environment remains on your system after the deletion.

This cleanup is beneficial for maintaining disk space and managing environments systematically without leaving unused packages and configurations behind. If you need the environment again in the future with the same packages, you would need to recreate it and reinstall the packages.
